notes.adapter_soroswap: Deployed 2026-09-12T17:29:00Z (third instance — see below), targets a real live Soroswap router (CCJUD55AG6W5HAI5LRVNKAE5WDP5XGZBUDS5WNTIVDU7O264UZZE7BRD) and pair (CDVAIOYHCD4RUSLQNVFI7RIZBFT2JZMJWM4RTOLQZQXL4QAVXU5RFKDB) on testnet, LP-ing native XLM against real testnet USDC (CB3TLW74NBIOT3BUWOZ3TUM6RFDF6A4GVIRUQRQZABG5KPOUL4JJOV2F). Registered as an ADDITIONAL strategy on the existing strategy_router (multi-strategy, alongside adapter_blend) - vault and router were not redeployed. Earns real trading fees as a liquidity provider, a genuinely different yield source from adapter_blend's lending supply. Two prior instances (CBNGHOQGI7YAMEQWFBB7Q4KWIAS6DJQJYQZHAFZIFREI3EQGGP4JJABR, CCEQBF2MGRM6AEJRWQAZXXWAYTCLPBWEKX3FP4TVQOVJ2UQMYQEKDD5E) are stale, superseded by two real bugs found via real failed testnet transactions (never a passing local test masking either — mock_all_auths_allowing_non_root_auth bypasses both classes entirely): (1) a two-hop cross-contract authorization gap — a contract's self-authorization is NOT automatic when it's two calls deep (adapter -> router -> token), fixed with env.authorize_as_current_contract(); (2) a compounding floor-division rounding bug in add_liquidity's sizing — passing an already-derived (rounded) amount as amount_a_desired made the router re-derive the other side from that already-rounded number, landing 1 unit below what had been pre-authorized; fixed by always passing the full, real, unrounded amounts to the router and only using the derived prediction for the pre-authorization. Real end-to-end exercise on this final instance (2026-09-12): allocated 50,000,000 stroops via update_debt, real swap of 25,000,000 XLM for 2,446,768 real testnet USDC, real add_liquidity minting 7,605,432 real LP tokens, total_value() = 49,850,221 (the ~0.3% gap from 50,000,000 is the real AMM swap fee, not an error).
